grammar.label: writing for a hostile reader
grammar.form: anticipating the objection in the sentence that invites it
grammar.meaning: survives a reader looking for a reason to dismiss you

explanation.en: A hostile reader reads every sentence for the weakest available interpretation, so the question is not whether a sentence can be read charitably but whether it can be read badly. Writing for that reader improves prose generally, which is the one consolation of it.
explanation.uz: Dushmanona o'quvchi har bir jumlani eng zaif ma'noda o'qiydi. Savol — jumlani yaxshi niyat bilan o'qish mumkinmi emas, balki yomon niyat bilan o'qish mumkinmi.

grammar.positive_example: I say 'two of the four districts' because 'half' would invite a fight I do not need.
grammar.negative_example: I say 'half the districts', which is true and shorter.

l1_notes.uz: Dushmanona o'quvchi uchun yozish — huquqiy va siyosiy matnlarda muhim ko'nikma.

grammar.label: conceding a point and losing nothing
grammar.form: the full concession followed by the narrowed claim
grammar.meaning: gives ground on a real point while holding the position that matters

explanation.en: The strongest move in an argument is to concede completely and then show the concession does not reach your claim. 'You are right that the sample is small. My claim is about direction, not magnitude.' Half-conceding invites the opponent to press; conceding fully and narrowing ends the line.
explanation.uz: Bahsdagi eng kuchli harakat — to'liq yon berish va keyin bu yon berish da'vongga yetmasligini ko'rsatish. Yarim yon berish raqibni bosishga undaydi.

grammar.positive_example: You are right that the sample is small. My claim is about direction, not size.
grammar.negative_example: The sample is small, but I think the result is probably still roughly right.

l1_notes.uz: To'liq yon berib, keyin da'voni toraytirish — ingliz bahs madaniyatidagi kuchli usul.

body.text: The district will read this line and stop reading.

body.speaker: Dilnoza
body.text: 'The district failed to check the figures.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Every word of it is true, and you are right. Somebody who has already decided I am against them will stop at that sentence.

body.speaker: Dilnoza
body.text: Then how do you write it?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I put their strongest point first, in their own words, and I concede it in full.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That two of the four districts did check, and that nobody gave any of them the staff to do it. I write that and I mean it.

body.speaker: Dilnoza
body.text: And then the finding sits in a paragraph they have already agreed with.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Which is the only place it will survive.

body.speaker: Dilnoza
body.text: Do you lose anything by conceding?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Only if the concession is false. Half a concession is worse than none: they can hear it, and now they do not trust the rest.

body.speaker: Dilnoza
body.text: And if they stop reading anyway?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Then I have written it for the committee instead, and the committee will notice that I was fair.
